title: Why Your Deep Research Agent Fails? On Hallucination Evaluation in Full Research Trajectory
abstract: arXiv:2601.22984v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Diagnosing failure patterns in Deep Research Agents (DRAs) remains a critical challenge. Existing benchmarks predominantly rely on end-to-end evaluation, obscuring intermediate hallucinations that accumulate throughout the research trajectory. To bridge this gap, we propose a shift from outcome-based to process-aware evaluation by auditing hallucinations in the full plan-search-summarize trajectory. We introduce the PING Taxonomy, which categorizes DRA hallucinations into four complementary types: Propagation, Intent, Noise-induced, and Grounding. We further instantiate this taxonomy into a fine-grained evaluation framework that decomposes trajectories into atomic actions, claims, and sub-queries for rigorous verification, and we validate its reliability on standard fact-checking benchmarks and human-reviewed trajectories. translated_title: 为什么你的深度研究智能体会失败？论完整研究轨迹中的幻觉评估
translated_abstract: 诊断深度研究智能体的失败模式仍然是一个关键挑战。现有基准主要依赖端到端评估，掩盖了在整个研究轨迹中累积的中间幻觉。为了弥补这一差距，我们提出从基于结果的评估转向过程感知的评估，通过审计完整的“规划-搜索-总结”轨迹中的幻觉。我们引入了PING分类法，将深度研究智能体的幻觉分为四种互补类型：传播型、意图型、噪声诱发型和接地型。我们进一步将该分类法实例化为一个细粒度评估框架，将轨迹分解为原子动作、声明和子查询以进行严格验证，并在标准事实核查基准和人工审查的轨迹上验证了其可靠性。利用该框架隔离出100个易产生幻觉的任务（包括对抗性场景），我们构建了D……
tldr: 该论文提出PING分类法和细粒度过程感知评估框架，将深度研究智能体的幻觉评估从仅看最终结果转向审计完整的“规划-搜索-总结”轨迹，从而诊断出在端到端评估中被掩盖的中间幻觉问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the PING Taxonomy and a fine-grained process-aware evaluation framework that audits hallucinations across the full plan-search-summarize trajectory of Deep Research Agents, shifting hallucination diagnosis from outcome-based evaluation to revealing intermediate failures hidden by end-to-end benchmarks.
